source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Two 3B base models got the same RL on Countdown. Qwen improved a lot, Llama little. Qwen already showed four Polya-like behaviours: verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining. Priming Llama with these behaviours closed the gap.
numbers: Countdown, PPO 250 steps: Qwen-2.5-3B ends near 60% accuracy, Llama-3.2-3B near 30%. Priming with the behaviours lets Llama match or beat Qwen.
quote: Qwen naturally shows these behaviors, while Llama initially lacks them.
limits: Countdown is a narrow arithmetic game; 3B models only; RL strengthened backtracking and verification but suppressed backward chaining and subgoal setting when all four were primed, so those two may be less useful here.
agent_relevance: Heuristic behaviours (work backwards, subgoal) are a measurable precondition for gains from extra compute. Supports O1-O5 as behaviours to elicit, but backward chaining itself was dropped by RL in this task.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners (controls)
finding: Controls rule out 'just more tokens'. An empty chain of thought and a length-matched placeholder chain gave no benefit; training on the empty chain even stopped Qwen exploring.
numbers: Empty-CoT and length-matched placeholder priming: Llama stays at the base 30-35% on Countdown.
limits: Single task and model family.
agent_relevance: Extra thinking time without heuristic structure does not help. A scaffold must add structure, not length.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners (incorrect solutions)
finding: Priming with solutions that showed the behaviours but had wrong answers worked as well as priming with correct solutions. Behaviour pattern mattered more than answer correctness.
numbers: Incorrect-answer all-strategies priming reached performance identical to correct-answer priming on Countdown (Fig. 6).
limits: Countdown only; Claude-3.5-Sonnet generated the traces and was often wrong.
agent_relevance: Process form (how one searches) can be taught separately from content correctness. G2/G3 still need real checks at test time.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners (pretraining test)
finding: In OpenWebMath and FineMath, verification and backtracking are rare (200,000 documents classified with Qwen-2.5-32B). Continued pretraining on a behaviour-enriched subset let Llama match Qwen after RL; a behaviour-minimised control did not.
numbers: 200,000 sampled documents; enriched Llama roughly equals Qwen, control shows limited improvement.
limits: Classifier was an LLM; effect shown on Countdown RL, not broad math.
agent_relevance: Human heuristic habits are scarce in ordinary maths text, which is a reason an explicit scaffold adds something.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction
finding: Step-back prompting asks first for the underlying principle (generalise), then reasons from it. It beat zero-shot CoT on physics and chemistry multiple choice.
numbers: MMLU Physics / Chemistry: PaLM-2L 66.4 / 70.9, +CoT 65.0 / 75.3, +Step-Back 73.2 / 81.8. GPT-4 + CoT 82.9 / 85.3, +Step-Back 84.5 / 85.6. Llama2-70B 51.9 / 55.7 to 64.8 / 66.7. 5 runs each.
limits: Gains over CoT are small for GPT-4 (about 1.6 points on Physics, 0.3 on Chemistry).
agent_relevance: Generalising to a principle first is a cheap O-type step, but the gain over CoT on a strong model is small.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction (GSM8K and error analysis)
finding: On GSM8K, step-back gave no gain over simple CoT, because the principles (add, subtract) are trivial. Errors after step-back are mostly in the reasoning step, not the abstraction step.
numbers: GSM8K PaLM-2L: plain 75.8, CoT 84.4, Step-Back 84.3. MMLU Physics: fixes 20.5% of base errors, introduces 11.9% new errors. Over 90% of remaining errors are reasoning errors; principle errors are a small fraction.
limits: Boundary: abstraction helps only when the problem needs a nontrivial principle.
agent_relevance: Use generalise/step-back only when a principle must be recalled; do not force it on routine arithmetic (G1).

source: Jiang et al. (2024) Forward-Backward Reasoning in Large Language Models for Mathematical Verification (FOBAR)
finding: Working backward as verification: mask a number in the question, give a candidate answer, ask the model to recover the masked number. Combining this with forward self-consistency voting beat voting alone.
numbers: Average over six math sets, CoT prompts: text-davinci-003 Self-Consistency 81.4 vs FOBAR 83.5; GPT-3.5-Turbo 85.5 vs 86.6; GPT-4 91.1 vs 91.4. GSM8K GPT-4 94.8 vs 95.4. Self-Verification (Weng) was worse than voting: 75.8 average on davinci.
limits: Gain shrinks as the model gets stronger (2.1 points, 1.1, 0.3). Needs a numeric masked value. With davinci+ComplexCoT, GSM8K was 79.1 for voting and 78.7 for FOBAR (no gain).
agent_relevance: Backward check is a real, template-based O-step with measured gain, largest for weaker models. Fits G3 (check against something the answer was not fitted to).

source: Chen et al. (2024) Reverse Thinking Makes LLMs Stronger Reasoners (RevThink)
finding: Training a student on forward reasoning plus a backward question and backward reasoning (from a teacher model) beat standard distillation across 12 datasets.
numbers: Average gain 13.53% over student zero-shot, 6.84% over best distillation baseline. Mistral-7B avg 50.55 zero-shot to 63.23; Gemma-7B 46.80 to 61.17. MATH: Mistral 10.42 to 15.28; GSM8K 54.71 to 60.88 (Answer Aug 59.08). 10% of training data beat plain SFT with full data on StrategyQA.
limits: Math gains are small relative to Answer Augmentation (Gemma GSM8K 57.21 vs AnsAug 57.37, a loss). Biggest gains on date and commonsense tasks, not math. Requires fine-tuning, not a prompt.
agent_relevance: Backward thinking helps most outside pure arithmetic; for math it is roughly a wash against good data augmentation.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Changing only names and numbers in GSM8K templates lowers and widens accuracy for most of 25 models. Original GSM8K scores often sit on the high side of the new distribution, hinting at contamination.
numbers: Spread between best and worst of 50 instantiations reaches 12% and more for many models (about 15% in the text). GSM8K score lies more than one SD from the GSM-Symbolic centre for 21 of 25 models. Drop negligible for GPT-4o and Llama3-8b.
limits: Not all models drop; frontier models are close to flat. Contamination is a hypothesis, not shown.
agent_relevance: Our benchmark gains must be tested on variants (G3). Specialising to new numbers is exactly the check that exposes pattern matching.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic (distractor test, GSM-NoOp)
finding: Adding one clause that looks relevant but changes nothing crashed accuracy. Models tend to turn 'discount' into multiplication regardless of context.
numbers: GSM-NoOp: drops up to 65% for Phi-3-mini; o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1, GPT-4o-mini -40.0 (accuracy points, Fig. 8).
limits: Frontier reasoning models are less hurt, but still hurt.
agent_relevance: Models fail the first Polya step, understanding the problem. A restate-and-strip-irrelevant step is motivated; test it, since the paper shows the failure but not a fix.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic (difficulty)
finding: Accuracy falls and variance rises as clauses are added to a question; the rate of drop speeds up with difficulty.
numbers: Fig. 6 shows decline across all tested models as the number of clauses grows (exact numbers per model only in figures).
limits: Numbers only in figures.
agent_relevance: Longer multi-step problems need decomposition and a stepwise check; single pass is fragile.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: Irrelevant sentences lowered accuracy a lot for all prompting methods, including least-to-most. An instruction to ignore irrelevant info and self-consistency each helped partly.
numbers: GSM-IC-4K: fewer than 30% of base problems are solved consistently after distractors (macro accuracy). text-davinci-003 base accuracy 80.0 (CoT) and 81.0 (least-to-most). Role-overlap distractors drove macro accuracy to 0 for text-davinci-003 in some cases.
limits: 2022-era models; later models improved (see GSM-NoOp).
agent_relevance: Same lesson earlier: the 'understand the problem' stage is a weak point and has a documented partial fix (instruction to ignore).

source: Chen et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with LLMs
finding: Reordering the statements of a problem, without changing the answer, harms accuracy. Presenting premises in proof order helps most. Preferences for other orders differ: GPT-4-turbo prefers backward order; PaLM 2-L does worst with backward order.
numbers: Logic task: permuting premises drops accuracy by over 30%; Gemini 1.0 Pro and GPT-3.5-turbo fall from above 65% to below 25%. R-GSM: GPT-4-turbo 94.1 to 85.0, PaLM 2-L 86.4 to 79.5, Gemini 1.0 Pro 80.5 to 69.1, GPT-3.5-turbo 67.3 to 51.8. On items originally solved: 89.9, 87.9, 74.6, 64.9.
limits: Mixed on backward chaining: it helps one model and hurts another. R-GSM is small and hand-written.
agent_relevance: Reordering the problem is a cheap robustness check (a mutated input, G3) and tests whether the model really works backward.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting
finding: Zero-shot 'devise a plan then carry it out' prompting reduces missing-step errors compared with zero-shot CoT. This is Polya's plan step in a prompt.
numbers: text-davinci-003 six arithmetic sets: CoT 70.4 average, PS 73.5 (PS table row 72.9 for one variant), PS+ 76.7, manual few-shot CoT 77.6. GSM8K: CoT 56.4, PS+ 59.3. Error analysis of 46 cases: 7% calculation, 12% missing step, 27% semantic misunderstanding.
limits: Gain on GSM8K only 2.9 points; one old model.
agent_relevance: A plan step helps a little; most errors (27%) are semantic misunderstanding, which a plan does not fix.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-Most Prompting
finding: Decompose into easier subproblems, solve in order feeding earlier answers forward. Large gain on length generalisation where CoT fails.
numbers: SCAN length split, code-davinci-002: least-to-most 99.7%, chain-of-thought 16.2% (standard prompt 16.7%).
limits: Gains hold on structured symbolic tasks; on distractor math (GSM-IC) least-to-most has lower macro accuracy than CoT for text-davinci-003.
agent_relevance: Decomposition shines when subproblems are easier than the whole in a way that generalises to longer instances.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: Meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models. CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks; on MMLU almost all of the gain comes from questions with an equals sign.
numbers: Up to 95% of CoT gain on MMLU from questions containing '='. GSM8K gain up to 66.9, MATH up to 41.6 points over direct answer. Planning-then-executing with a symbolic solver beats CoT for both steps.
limits: Gain is mostly in symbolic execution, not in planning; a solver beats CoT.
agent_relevance: Heuristic-style reasoning pays on math and symbolic items; hand arithmetic to code and do not force deliberation on other items (G1).

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 labels math questions with skills; showing the model exemplars tagged with the chosen skill improves accuracy.
numbers: MATH: +11.6% over CoT, +3.5% over Complex CoT and over a topic-based baseline; +7.52% over PAL code solutions; +4.0% over CoT with self-consistency.
limits: Skill labels come from the same family of models; MATH and GSM8K only.
agent_relevance: Naming the needed technique first, then retrieving matched worked examples, is a measured mechanism for O-operators.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Having the model recall related problems before solving (a Polya 'have you seen a related problem' step) beat zero-shot and few-shot CoT.
numbers: Average accuracy gain about +4% over baselines on GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench; GSM8K with GPT-3.5-turbo about 75 to 78 across methods (table garbled in extraction).
limits: Gain on GSM8K is small; self-generated exemplars vary in quality.
agent_relevance: Related-problem recall works without human exemplars.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover
finding: Model selects, adapts and implements reasoning modules into a task-level structure. Beat direct answering and CoT on most Big-Bench Hard tasks with far fewer calls.
numbers: PaLM 2-L: beats direct answering on 23 of 25 tasks and CoT on 21 of 25; up to 32% over CoT; 10-40x fewer inference calls than inference-heavy methods. On MATH 74.7% of failures are computation errors; wrong reasoning structure 25.3%.
limits: Gains weakest on algorithmic and maths items where execution errors dominate.
agent_relevance: Picking a heuristic is not the bottleneck on math; executing it is. Pair with code execution.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning
finding: Eight chain-of-thought exemplars gave state-of-the-art GSM8K accuracy with PaLM 540B; gains appear only at large scale.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K: roughly 18% standard vs 57% with CoT (from Figure 2, not in extracted text, so approximate).
limits: Emerges with scale. Foundation for all prompt-level heuristics.
agent_relevance: Baseline against which every heuristic prompt must be compared.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without outside feedback, asking the model to review and fix its answer does not help and often hurts. With oracle labels it helps a lot.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 standard, 75.1 after round 1, 74.7 after round 2. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1. With oracle: GPT-4 GSM8K 97.5.
limits: Oracle labels leak the answer; earlier positive results used them. Models change correct answers to wrong ones.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: revise only with real output. The control stage of Schoenfeld needs an external check.

source: Lightman et al. (2024) Let's Verify Step by Step
finding: A reward model trained on step-level human labels picked better solutions than one trained on final-answer labels.
numbers: MATH representative subset, best-of-1860: process-supervised 78.2% solved, outcome-supervised 72.4%, majority voting 69.6%.
limits: Needs 800K human step labels (PRM800K); MATH only.
agent_relevance: Checking each step beats checking the end; a code-run step check is the cheap version.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) A Careful Examination of LLM Performance on Grade School Arithmetic (GSM1k)
finding: A new 1,000-problem GSM8K-style set shows that some model families score lower than on GSM8K; frontier models do not.
numbers: Drops up to 8%; Spearman r2 = 0.36 between a model's likelihood of generating GSM8K items and its GSM8K-GSM1k gap. Phi, Mistral and some Llama overfit; Gemini, GPT and Claude show little.
limits: All models still generalise to new problems; correlation is modest.
agent_relevance: Gains from heuristic prompting must be tested on fresh items, not on public sets.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Reasoning models face a complexity cliff on puzzles such as Tower of Hanoi, and reasoning effort drops at high complexity despite spare token budget. Three regimes: standard models better at low complexity, thinking models at medium, both fail at high.
numbers: Hanoi: N=1-4 accuracy declines with longer reasoning (overthinking), N=5-7 improves, N>=8 near zero.
limits: Disputed: see next line.
agent_relevance: Thinking models do not reliably execute a known algorithm; hand execution to code.

source: Lawsen (2025) The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking
finding: A rebuttal says the Hanoi collapse mostly reflects output-token limits and impossible River Crossing cases (N>=6 boat capacity), not reasoning failure. Asking for a generating function gave high accuracy on Hanoi cases scored as failures.
numbers: Preliminary tests on several models only; no table of numbers in the comment.
limits: Short comment, not peer reviewed; tests are preliminary and partly from a social-media replication.
agent_relevance: Failure on long exact outputs can be an output-budget artefact; score with code-run answers.

source: Schoenfeld (1985) Mathematical Problem Solving, Heuristics chapter
finding: Explicit heuristic training with college students improved problem solving over untrained controls, but only when heuristics were broken into specific operational strategies, not left as Polya's labels. Polya's headings were descriptions, not procedures a novice can run.
numbers: Not recorded.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Small studies; transfer far from taught problems is weak.
agent_relevance: Each O-operator needs a concrete template and practice; the label alone is not enough.

source: Schoenfeld (1985) Mathematical Problem Solving, Control chapter
finding: Video study of novices: a large share spent the whole attempt on one approach and never checked progress, while experts monitored and switched. Control decisions, not knowledge, separated them.
numbers: Recalled as about 60% of novice attempts of the 'read, choose, pursue, no monitoring' kind.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Small sample of protocols.
agent_relevance: Basis for S6 control and the impasse detector. Verify the 60% figure before citing.

source: Begle (1979) Critical Variables in Mathematics Education; Lester (1994) Musings about mathematical problem-solving research 1970-1994
finding: Reviews of 1970s studies found that teaching generic heuristics rarely improved problem solving, which motivated Schoenfeld's argument for specific, practised strategies and control.
numbers: Not recorded.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Secondary recall; reviews of mixed-quality studies.
agent_relevance: Prior evidence on generic heuristics is weak; do not assume prompt-level heuristics transfer.

source: Hembree (1992) Experiments and relational studies in problem solving: a meta-analysis
finding: Meta-analysis of problem-solving instruction: heuristic and strategy instruction had a positive mean effect, with diagrams and long practised instruction among the stronger factors.
numbers: Effect sizes not recorded.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Mixed designs and dated.
agent_relevance: Diagrams and sustained practice matter more than brief reminders.

source: Kramarski and Mevarech (2003) IMPROVE metacognitive questioning
finding: Metacognitive questioning (comprehension, connection, strategy, reflection) improved mathematical reasoning more than cooperative learning without it.
numbers: Effect sizes not recorded.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Classroom studies, mostly eighth grade.
agent_relevance: Four self-questions are a template for S6 monitoring, with human evidence.

source: Sinha and Kapur (2021) When problem solving followed by instruction works: productive failure meta-analysis
finding: Attempting a problem before instruction beat instruction first for conceptual understanding and transfer, when design features were present.
numbers: Recalled: Hedges g about 0.36 overall, higher with high-fidelity design.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Effect depends on how instruction is delivered.
agent_relevance: Trying before being told the method may help generalisation; relevant to when to apply heuristics.

source: Kirschner, Sweller and Clark (2006) Why minimal guidance during instruction does not work
finding: Argues explicit guidance beats discovery for novices; worked examples help.
numbers: No effect sizes; argument paper.
limits: Not opened this session; recalled from memory, verify before use. Contested by later work.
agent_relevance: Competing explanation: guidance helps novices; heuristics can hurt experts (expertise reversal).
